subject: Outbound follow-up template review (PLG signals pilot) — copy + guardrails
body:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Outbound follow-up template review (PLG signals pilot) — copy + guardrails

Hi Ben + Steph —

Attaching the latest draft sequences for the PLG signal pilot. These are meant to be “good enough” for week 1 while we gather replies/objections and tune.

What I need from you today:
1) Any wording that feels too assumptive/creepy (e.g., “saw you hit 429s”) vs the right level of specificity.
2) Any claim that needs proof/benchmarking language (I tried to avoid hard numbers).
3) Positioning tweaks for Hosted → Dedicated vs Hosted → Private paths.

We’re using a 1/3/7/14-day cadence, primarily email with a light LI touch where appropriate.

Attachments:
- SDR_Sequence_Drafts_PLG_Signals_v3.docx
- Personalization_Tokens_and_Snippets_v1.txt

Thanks,
Grace
—
Grace O'Connor
SDR Program Owner | Redwood Inference


From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Outbound follow-up template review (PLG signals pilot) — copy + guardrails

Grace — this is strong and reads human (thank you).

Edits/suggestions (mostly risk + tone):
- Avoid “we noticed” in the first line. It can feel surveill-y. Suggest: “Some teams hit this as they scale…” and then offer help diagnosing.
- Keep “rate limits / throughput / residency / security review” framed as common inflection points, not as something we definitively observed.
- Add opt-out language to the last touch (Day 14) that’s explicit but short (“If this isn’t relevant, reply ‘no’ and I’ll close the loop.”). This reduces complaints.

For the “pricing page” / “docs” engagement variants: I’d keep those as the least specific trigger (“Saw you checking out Dedicated options”) vs “you visited X page 4 times.”

I’ll do a pass in-line on the doc if you want, but the above are the main ones.

Ben
—
Ben Carter
Growth Marketing | Redwood Inference


From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 10:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: Outbound follow-up template review (PLG signals pilot) — copy + guardrails

+1 to Ben.

Sales leadership feedback (what will help reps + what will hurt):

1) Remove infra assumptions.
A few lines imply they’re on Kubernetes / self-hosting GPUs (“when you’re managing your own clusters…”). Many of these are pure API users. Recommend keeping it: “as traffic grows, teams usually need either reserved throughput or private networking.”

2) Add one sentence that anchors why we’re reaching out.
Not “we tracked you,” but a credible “why now”: “We’re seeing your usage scale and wanted to share best practices + options before reliability becomes the bottleneck.”

3) Clear CTA options.
Make the CTA binary: 15 min to sanity-check, or “not a priority” and we’ll stop. Avoid multiple asks (call + questionnaire + demo).

4) Dedicated vs Private routing.
- Dedicated email should lead with predictable throughput + isolation + cost per token.
- Private email should lead with VPC/on-prem, audit logs, SSO/SAML, residency.

If you want, I can give you two approved subject lines per track. For now, I’d avoid anything that says “urgent” or “action required.”

Steph
—
Stephanie Nguyen
VP Sales, North America | Redwood Inference


From: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 11:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Outbound follow-up template review (PLG signals pilot) — copy + guardrails

Quick ops note so we don’t create attribution chaos later:

- Please keep the “trigger” language consistent across variants (same phrasing) so we can map replies by sequence type.
- Don’t include any dynamic tokens that might accidentally insert user-level identifiers (names from telemetry, etc.). Domain + company name only.
- If we’re adding an opt-out line, let’s standardize it across sequences so we can filter “opt-out” responses reliably.

Also: if you’re planning LI touches, please add a short tag to the doc indicating which touches have a LI step so we can set expectations with the SDRs.

Tyler
—
Tyler Benson
Marketing Ops | Redwood Inference


From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 1:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Outbound follow-up template review (PLG signals pilot) — copy + guardrails

This is super helpful. I’m making these changes now:

- Replace “we noticed / saw” with “teams often run into…” + “happy to compare notes if helpful.”
- Remove any Kubernetes/cluster language.
- Add a single “why now” line (usage scaling) without citing the exact signal.
- Tighten CTA to 15-min check-in OR “not a priority.”
- Add standardized opt-out on Day 14.

Two questions:
1) For “rate-limit pain” — do we want to mention 429s explicitly anywhere, or keep it generic as “rate limits / throughput constraints”? My instinct is generic.
2) For Private/security intent — is it okay to say “if you’re heading into a security review” or is that too assumptive?

If you can send the two approved subject lines per track, I’ll incorporate.

Grace


From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 2:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Outbound follow-up template review (PLG signals pilot) — copy + guardrails

Jumping in with the exec POV since we’ll get forwarded to prospects.

- Do NOT mention “429” or “error rate” in outbound. Keep it to “scaling / reliability / throughput constraints” and offer to help diagnose.
- For Private: “If you’re evaluating security/compliance requirements (SSO, audit logs, residency)” is safer than “heading into a security review.” Let them self-identify.
- On the “why now”: keep it as “we’re reaching out because some teams at your usage stage start thinking about…” That’s defensible.

Steph — yes on the subject lines; please share with Grace.

Grace — ship with the edits above. Better to be slightly less specific and protect trust.

Jordan
—
Jordan Blake
CRO | Redwood Inference
